setlist_extra.title: This Could Be The Last Time

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Foolish Heart** (3 reviews): Works well as a first-set closer; Rated a top-three version, with echoes of Bertha, Franklin's Tower and Scarlet Begonias; open-ended [16][18][22]
- **Easy To Love You** (1 review): Brent was on fire during this song [19]
- **The Weight** (1 other source): The audience source has a roughly quarter-second cut about two minutes in [5]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Brent entered late, after the band hit the downbeat hard [20]

## The recordings

- **gd90-05-06.sbd.wiley.11661.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 173 min; rated 4.04/5 by 26 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says an analog copy sounds better than this soundboard, which suffers generational loss; Tape copies sound flat; reviewer thinks the board recordings of the Carson run came out that way; The soundboard sounds flat [12][17][18]
- **gd1990-05-06.mtx.hansokolow.97237.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 174 min [5]
- **gd1990-05-06.141940.FOB.Schoeps.BK.Mattes.Miler.Noel.t-flac1648**: source not stated; 20 songs; 174 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [9]
- **gd1990-05-06.141263.sbd.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 20 songs; 171 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [2]

## Around the show

- The usual South Bay spring marine layer failed to roll in on either day [14]
- Weir asked the crowd for a moment of silence for the Celtics [16]
- Long, hot wait of about 90 degrees, then a long run to the stage once gates opened [19]
- Friday was mid-80s; Saturday and Sunday jumped to 105 and 108 degrees [20]
- Flat lawn and hot weather; a tall attendee halfway back could still see the stage [22]
- Timothy Leary, in a pink suit at the side of the stage, and Bill Walton were seen [23]
- Reviewer recalls extreme heat, about 103 degrees on Sunday, at these daytime shows [23]
- Tapers staked out a large quiet zone and waited in line in 106-degree sun [8]
- Blow Away is described as comparable to the previous day's version [14]
- Second-set surprises make the show special; reviewer recommends hearing both nights [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd90-05-06.sbd.wiley.11661.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>MC>DAT>CD [1]
- **gd1990-05-06.mtx.hansokolow.97237.flac16**: transferred by hansokolow; source: matrix of DSBD: shnid=80278 and DAUD: shnid=7891 by hansokolow using ProTools [5]. Also: Matrix made by hansokolow in ProTools from a soundboard DAT and audience DAT, with transfers by Charlie Miller; Audience DAT was slowed slightly to fit the soundboard, a common fix with DATs [5]
- **gd1990-05-06.141940.FOB.Schoeps.BK.Mattes.Miler.Noel.t-flac1648**: taped by Ted Mattes; transferred by Charlie Miller and Joe Noel; source: flac16/48kHz ; Ted Mattes Recording (FOB): Set I: Schoeps CMC4 MK2 > Grace preamp > DAT 48k; Set II: B+K 4011 > DAT 48k; Charlie Miller [9]
- **gd1990-05-06.141263.sbd.miller.flac2496**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-X90) [2]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Wolfgang's: [Grateful Dead Backstage Pass from Cal State Dominguez Hills, May 6, 1990 at Wolfgang's](https://www.wolfgangs.com/backstage-passes/grateful-dead/backstage-pass/CSD900506.html) [25]
- Poster by Wolfgang's: [Grateful Dead Backstage Pass from Cal State Dominguez Hills, May 6, 1990 at Wolfgang's](https://www.wolfgangs.com/backstage-passes/grateful-dead/backstage-pass/CSD900506.html) [26]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead California State U. Dominguez Hills - May 6, 1990](https://www.dead.net/show/may-6-1990) [27]
- Photo by a Flickr member (All rights reserved): [19900506_S16_36](https://www.flickr.com/photos/22038610@N00/3346464006/) [28]
- Photo by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/22038610@N00/3346464006/) [29]
